subject: Contract gating, acceptance testing schedule & order-form dependencies
messages:
From: Sara Miller <sara.miller@acme-robotics.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Erickson <tom.erickson@acme-robotics.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 15:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Evaluation plan kickoff + MAP template

Hi Aditya —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Tom and I sketched out a rough evaluation cadence and wanted to confirm the gating steps so we can align procurement timing. High level:

- Week 1 (pilot config): tooling access, non-prod data ingest, basic latency checks
- Week 2 (functional eval): quality checks on 3 core flows, acceptance prompts
- Week 3 (stress & throughput): concurrency at target QPS, KV cache behavior
- Week 4 (legal/procurement): finalize DPA language and order form to enable rollout

Two asks: can Redwood confirm which clause in the DPA we should expect to see redlined (data residency & subprocessor list) and whether an initial MSA signature can be decoupled from the order-form effective date? Procurement would like a clear list of dependent signoffs so they can run internal approvals.

Attached a first-pass MAP (spreadsheet) with milestones.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Miller
Sr. Program Manager, Platform Ops
Acme Robotics

Attachments: acme_map_v1.xlsx
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Miller <sara.miller@acme-robotics.com>
Cc: Tom Erickson <tom.erickson@acme-robotics.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Feb 2028 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Evaluation plan kickoff + MAP template

Sara —

Great write-up, and thanks for the MAP. I pulled a slightly annotated version (see Drive link) and added our recommended sequencing to reduce gating friction:

1) Execute MSA (commercial terms) with signature from both sides. This locks broad liability and onboarding responsibilities.
2) Staple DPA as an addendum but allow redlines to be delivered during Week 2 functional eval; we can accept a DPA with an agreed open-item list if your legal team provides it within the first 10 business days of the pilot.
3) Order form (billing/usage tiers) to be countersigned once acceptance criteria are met in Week 3 — this prevents procurement from paying upfront for scale before performance is validated.
4) Technical handoff & production cutover window scheduled post-order-form.

Practical notes:
- Redwood can provide an interim scoped SOC-2 extract and subprocessor list for your security review in parallel.
- If Acme requires MSA + order form to be signed together for procurement reasons, we can offer a staging clause that sets the order form effective date to the acceptance date (mutually agreed ramp).

Looping Laura (legal) to flag any non-starter DPA items and Karthik (solutions) to confirm the test harness we’ll use for Week 2 prompts.

Drive (annotated MAP): https://drive.google.com/rdw/acme-map-v1

Best,
Aditya Rao
Principal Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_dpa_clauses_v2.pdf
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Sara Miller <sara.miller@acme-robotics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Evaluation plan kickoff + MAP template

Aditya / Sara —

Quick legal read: the approach is workable but a couple of points to clarify so we don’t create downstream procurement blockers.

- DPA: Accept open-item list during pilot only if it includes (a) explicit subprocessor notice window, (b) a defined data retention cap for pilot artifacts, and (c) an agreed comms plan if an incident triggers. We can ship redline-friendly DPA v2.
- MSA: We prefer the MSA signed before any provision of credentials to production-like environments. For non-prod access (pilot only) we can permit limited scoped credentials under a mutual NDA addendum.
- Order form: Procurement at Acme will often demand a committed term to approve payment; if they insist on simultaneous signature, propose the staging clause Aditya mentioned. We should capture that in the MSA as a named clause ("Order-Form Effective Date Election").

Could Sara confirm whether Acme procurement requires an order-form signed before any spend is visible in their vendor system? That will determine whether we need a purchase-order-style invoice or can use the staging clause.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: (none)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Miller <sara.miller@acme-robotics.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 11:45:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Evaluation plan kickoff + MAP template

Sara —

Thanks — quick operations summary and ask from procurement side:

- Timeline alignment we need confirmed by EOD Friday (17 Feb):
  * Pilot start: Mon 20 Feb (we provision non-prod cluster, share creds)
  * Functional eval: 21–27 Feb (Redwood test harness + your sample prompts)
  * Throughput test: 28 Feb (scheduled load window, Redwood provides QPS script)
  * Acceptance review & sign: 1–2 Mar (acceptance runbook + sign-off form)

- Dependencies we will track in the MAP: MSA signed (either fully or with staging clause) -> limited non-prod creds -> DPA open items submitted -> order-form countersign after acceptance.
- Action items for Acme procurement: confirm whether their system requires a signed order form to create a PO (yes/no), and share expected procurement lead time once we hand them the draft order-form (in business days).

If procurement confirms they need the order form first, we will schedule an internal exec approval for the staging clause and prepare a short memo for your procurement approver to reduce cycles.

I’ll update the MAP spreadsheet and push a new version to Drive by EOD.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
